correctness.rationale: For any finite simple G, a selected induced subgraph of its full one-subdivision is acyclic iff selected old-old internal edge subdivisions form an acyclic graph on selected original vertices A; subdivisions incident to an omitted old vertex are leaves/isolated and cannot create cycles. Maximality forces all noninternal subdivision vertices to be selected, internal selected edges F to be a spanning tree of every connected component of G[A], and each omitted old x to have two neighbors in the same selected component, exactly the claimed iff. For K_n (n>=3), A must have size a>=2 and can be chosen arbitrarily; Cayley provides a^(a-2) internal spanning trees. Selected size N+2a-1-C(a,2); complement size n-2a+1+C(a,2). Exact finite recomputation n=3..8 recovers coefficients and extremal sizes. For n=4 the two facet sizes 7,8 prove nonpurity; first differences 2-a yield unbounded size gaps. Finite checks only corroborate the unrestricted cycle-suppression proof.

value.rationale: The maximal induced-forest complex and irredundant feedback-vertex-set spectrum differ from merely determining a minimum FVS size. The general subdivision iff enables exact structural enumeration; the natural complete-graph specialization gives all facet sizes, Cayley multiplicities, nonpurity threshold and arbitrary large gaps. These could serve topological or combinatorial researchers studying induced complexes.
